sequence.spoken_text: Open Workflows in the Chicago Fire demonstration department. We will build a training call-created workflow with two ordered actions and a separate call-closed workflow. Begin with the outcome you want and the event that should cause it. Each workflow listens to one event. Multiple steps can respond to that event, while a different event needs a different workflow.
sequence.purpose: Open the actual Workflows list and its navigation controls.

sequence.spoken_text: Inspect the list's event and enabled columns before editing, and identify who will monitor the result when the automation runs.
sequence.purpose: Use the populated final list to show each event and status; actual state is Disabled, not a first-visit claim.

sequence.spoken_text: Open Credentials and create Academy local captured mail.
sequence.purpose: Show Credentials and the stored training credential identity.

sequence.spoken_text: Choose SMTP Email. In this isolated exercise, Mailpit receives messages inside the training network; nothing goes to an outside mail service. Set the local host, port and demonstration sender, keep the unused password masked, and save.
sequence.purpose: Show actual credential type and safe local settings; do not substitute the stored list for these fields.

sequence.spoken_text: Your live department needs its own mail provider settings and appropriate transport security. The credential type must match the action. A stored credential supplies authentication details; it does not establish that a destination is reachable or accepts a message.
sequence.purpose: Keep the saved credential visible during the authentication-versus-delivery caution.

sequence.spoken_text: Choose New Workflow
sequence.purpose: Show New Workflow before entering setup.

sequence.spoken_text: and name it Academy call opened — captured mail. Select CallAdded as Trigger Event. Turn Enabled off while configuring the destination and actions, and review the retry controls.
sequence.purpose: Show the disabled create form, actual name, CallAdded and retry controls.

sequence.spoken_text: The event becomes fixed after creation, so confirm it before saving. Keep retry values modest for practice and observe actual attempt timing later.
sequence.purpose: Show literal fixed-event help after creation.

sequence.spoken_text: Template gallery examples also need their destinations and credentials completed before enabling.

sequence.spoken_text: Select Add Step.
sequence.purpose: Show the visible Add Step control.

sequence.spoken_text: Choose Send Email and set Order to one. Enter the fictional training-supervisor address and a subject, then select Academy local captured mail as the SMTP credential. In Output Template, use a short training message with department name and call name from the variable reference.
sequence.purpose: Show first action type, Order one, fictional supervisor destination, subject, credential and template variables.

sequence.spoken_text: Keep unnecessary personal details and narratives out of the message.
sequence.purpose: Keep the actual short department/call template visible during the data-minimization instruction.

sequence.spoken_text: Save the step and inspect its card in the editor. The card shows the action and a template excerpt; the execution history will show whether a send actually completed.
sequence.purpose: Show the saved first-step card and excerpt; no execution claim at this stage.

sequence.spoken_text: Add a second Send Email step at Order two.
sequence.purpose: Show Add Step and the actual second Send Email step Order two.

sequence.spoken_text: For this exercise, run it only when the call name contains TRAINING. Use Visual Builder for simple comparisons, or Raw Expression with Scriban braces. Here, call.name piped to string.contains TRAINING must render true for the step to run.
sequence.purpose: Show actual TRAINING expression and Visual Builder / Raw Expression tabs.

sequence.spoken_text: Select Test Condition and read the result carefully. A syntax-valid message means the expression can be read; without sample event data, it does not establish whether this call will pass.
